items.body:
Anthropic数学家宣称证明「数学界第一神山」黎曼猜想，市场质疑其「利好」发布动机

Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 发布声明，称自己与 AI 模型 Claude 合作，找到了黎曼猜想及广义黎曼猜想（GRH）的证明方法，并同步公布超过 1700 万行 Lean 形式化代码。由于声明发布恰逢 Anthropic 上市次日，这项数学突破也引发了外界对发布时间及商业动机的讨论。

Alpöge 将证明以 Lean 语言写成，分为 14 个压缩文件发布。与此同时，他与 Claude 生成的文字版证明超过 25 万页，但因篇幅过长、难以阅读而没有公开。

对此，2006 年菲尔兹奖得主陶哲轩在个人博客发文称，初步分析显示，这份证明似乎综合运用了朗兰兹纲领和算术几何领域的现代研究成果，验证工作预计还需要一段时间。

items.title: 特朗普称将对海外建AI数据中心的美企征税
items.summary: 当地时间11月20日，在白宫新闻简报室举行的记者会上，美国总统特朗普表示，若美国科技企业在海外建设数据中心，将面临“巨额税款”惩罚。他没有透露具体措施，还告诉记者，自己尚未将这一计划告知政府官员。 特朗普称，他希望美国企业把数据中心建在美国本土。“我们不会允许数据中心建到别的国家去，我们不会让这种事发生。哪个公司想这么做，我们就会对它征收巨额税款。”他说，美国人应该欢迎数据中心。 他补充道：“你们应该好好利用这些数据中心。让开发商给你们付钱，给你们的社区付钱，但别把他们拒之门外。我们希望他们把数据中心建在这里。” —— 观察者网
items.body:
特朗普称将对海外建AI数据中心的美企征税

当地时间11月20日，在白宫新闻简报室举行的记者会上，美国总统特朗普表示，若美国科技企业在海外建设数据中心，将面临“巨额税款”惩罚。他没有透露具体措施，还告诉记者，自己尚未将这一计划告知政府官员。

特朗普称，他希望美国企业把数据中心建在美国本土。“我们不会允许数据中心建到别的国家去，我们不会让这种事发生。哪个公司想这么做，我们就会对它征收巨额税款。”他说，美国人应该欢迎数据中心。

他补充道：“你们应该好好利用这些数据中心。让开发商给你们付钱，给你们的社区付钱，但别把他们拒之门外。我们希望他们把数据中心建在这里。”

—— 观察者网

items.title: How Watch Duty is using Gemini to get wildfire alerts out faster
items.summary: Watch Duty uses Gemini to turn noisy fire radio into text, spotting wildfire dispatches in under 30 seconds so alerts go out faster.
items.body:
How Watch Duty is using Gemini to get wildfire alerts out faster

Built with pro bono support from a Google.org Fellowship, a new Gemini-powered tool turns noisy fire radio into real-time text, helping Watch Duty spot new wildfire dispatches in under 30 seconds.

Eve Andersson

Senior Director for Social Impact

Stephanie Chew

Software Engineer

Listen to article

[[duration]] minutes

This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental

This July, as the Railroad Fire spread through Washington overnight, Watch Duty sent its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert to its users. It started with a 911 dispatch buried in radio static — and a new Gemini tool that caught it in seconds.

A dedicated team of Google engineers and researchers spent six months embedded full-time with Watch Duty, a nonprofit wildfire alert app run by active and retired firefighters, dispatchers, and first responders. Through the Google.org Fellowship, they used more than 20,000 hours of past radio recordings to build a Gemini-powered tool that wipes out heavy static and translates specialized firefighting terminology into clean, searchable text. The system removes the added strain of deciphering noisy audio so volunteers can focus on verifying incidents and getting alerts out.

The challenge

When a wildfire starts, minutes can decide whether people get out safely. Yet across much of the country, the first word of a new fire still travels over decades-old analog VHF radio, where engine noise, wind, static, and rapid-fire tactical jargon make it hard to hear what's happening. Watch Duty reporters monitor up to 20 feeds manually, making it a challenge to cut through the noise.

The results

Across Watch Duty's network, the tool has:

• Helped close coverage gaps in areas with no other automated dispatch detection, sending reporters a signal in less than 30 seconds; this way, a new fire isn't missed just because no one was listening at that moment

• Reduced word error rate on degraded VHF radio audio from 38% down to 22.34%

• Transcribed more than 200 hours of radio speech a day from about 400 active feeds, and has been designed and tested to handle more than 10,000 feeds at once.

As a result of the collaboration between Google and Watch Duty, volunteer reporter satisfaction with radio transcription tools increased from 35.3% to 92.3%.

The tool was also put to test during a live fire. In July 2026, a fast-moving wildfire — the Railroad Fire — ignited at night in Washington. When the first 911 dispatch went out over local fire radio, the Gemini-powered transcription tool transcribed it straight from the noisy radio audio and flagged it in under 30 seconds.

That head start gave Watch Duty's team the time they needed to verify the fire and push a Critical Alert—which breaks through do-not-disturb mode in urgent situations—helping residents evacuate before flames reached homes. It was the first time Watch Duty had ever sent a Critical Alert overnight, proving what faster detection means when communities are asleep and every minute counts.

The collaboration

The new AI radio tool is the latest milestone in a deep, multi-year collaboration spanning Google's philanthropic, product, and research teams to help Watch Duty scale its life-saving mission across all 50 states.

• Funding: In 2024, Google.org provided Watch Duty with $2 million in funding and $300,000 in Google Cloud credits to help compile satellite, camera, and radio data to validate new fires.

• Search: During US fires such as the Palisades, Eaton, Hurst, and Auto fires, Google Search featured Watch Duty in SOS alerts alongside official emergency guidance.

• Alerts at scale: Watch Duty sends push alerts through Firebase Cloud Messaging. As its audience grew to more than 16 million people last year, Google Cloud raised its messaging limit from 600,000 to 1 million to help alerts arrive without delay.

• Broader industry partnership: As part of the AI Collaborative: Wildfires, Watch Duty is turning models and data into tools that agencies, communities, and responders trust and use.

When the next fire starts, the goal is simple: get people the warning they need while there's still time to act.

It was the first time Watch Duty had ever sent a Critical Alert overnight, proving what faster detection means when communities are asleep and every minute counts.
The collaboration

The new AI radio tool is the latest milestone in a deep, multi-year collaboration spanning Google's philanthropic, product, and research teams to help Watch Duty scale its life-saving mission across all 50 states.

Broader industry partnership: As part of the AI Collaborative: Wildfires, Watch Duty is turning models and data into tools that agencies, communities, and responders trust and use.

items.body:
SpaceX旗下Cursor考虑弃用中国AI模型，众议院报告施压引发替代潮

据 CNBC 报道，SpaceX 旗下 AI 编程平台 Cursor 正考虑因「地缘政治风险」逐步淘汰中国开发的开放权重 AI 模型。报告指出，Cursor 的编程模型 Composer 2 正是基于月之暗面的 Kimi K2.5 构建。SpaceX 于今年 8 月以隐含 600 亿美元的估值完成对 Cursor 的收购。该报告经过数月调查，发现成本、定制化能力及接近前沿的性能，是推动美国科技公司采用中国模型的核心原因，这引发了华盛顿的担忧。

报告指出，美国目前缺乏在「市场价格和性能」上具备竞争力的开源权重替代品。为此报告建议启动一项「美国国家开放权重倡议」，整合公共算力与评估基础设施。此外还呼吁在 10 月禁止 DeepSeek 进入联邦民事机构系统的基础上，进一步禁止联邦信息系统及联邦合同使用中国开发的 AI 模型。除 Cursor 外，Airbnb 和 DoorDash 也因使用中国 AI 模型接受了调查。与此同时，美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）本周一发布了临时最终规则，声称目标防止中国公司通过海外数据中心远程访问美国 AI 芯片并利用其进行模型蒸馏。

北京拟明确租房正常损耗不得扣减押金

北京市住建委与市场监管局起草的《北京市住房租赁合同（示范文本）（修订征求意见稿）》20 日起公开征求意见，拟明确承租人正常使用造成的房屋正常损耗不承担赔偿责任，出租人不得以此为由扣减押金。

余承东，最新发声：发布会讲话不准确，现在还是 L2 时代，开车不能睡觉

11 月 20 日晚间，华为常务董事、终端 BG 董事长余承东发文回应“开车睡觉”相关言论，他称：“今天发布会上，有几句话讲得不准确，要纠正一下。享界 V8 现在给大家用的是 L2 辅助驾驶，L3 的硬件能力已具备，但还没有开放。大家用辅助驾驶要专心开车、按要求握好方向盘。现在还是 L2 时代，大家一定要注意安全，开车不能睡觉”。

证券时报

当天下午的鸿蒙智行享界 V8 及星芒品牌发布会上，他介绍 V8 率先开启全国首个 120 km/h L3 自动驾驶跨城高速路测，随后说「L3 自动驾驶来了以后，开车就不用摸方向盘了，开车是可以睡觉的，别睡死过去就行了，20 秒还是多少秒给你唤醒就可以了」，还提到系统搞不定时会安全停车、用安全带扽人、用喇叭喊起床。直播画面随即被切走，这番话很快引发争议。

items.body:
OpenAI跟进Anthropic防蒸馏措施：GPT-6.2思维链也上锁了

OpenAI 开始给 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 的隐藏思维链加锁，防止其他模型通过 API 偷走推理过程，用来训练自己的模型。这套机制与 Anthropic 先前推出的防蒸馏措施高度相似。

10 月底，《The Information》援引知情人士报道称，DeepSeek 和月之暗面在训练新模型时，大量使用了 GPT-6 Astra 的输出。此前，国内 AI 公司曾大量蒸馏 Claude，但 Anthropic 不断加强封堵，促使部分厂商把目标转向 OpenAI。

蒸馏就是让一个模型学习更强模型的输出，以较低成本获得类似能力。如果能拿到完整的思维链，连模型如何拆解问题、一步步得出答案都能学走，比只看最终答案更有价值。

Anthropic 今年 6 月已经给 Claude 的加密思维链加上「上下文锁」。OpenAI 如今也采用类似机制：在多轮对话中，每段推理都与生成它之前的历史消息绑定。如果开发者修改旧提示词、工具配置或对话内容，API 就可能丢弃改动位置之后的推理项，防止攻击者通过篡改上下文诱导模型泄露内部思考。

OpenAI 公布的自测结果显示，在尝试提取上一轮隐藏推理的攻击中，GPT-6 Astra 的平均攻击成功率高达 54%，GPT-6.2 Astra 降至 0.2%，Sol 为 0.5%。

正常开发者也会受到影响。修改旧消息或压缩聊天记录，可能导致 Agent 丢失之前的推理成果，增加 Token 消耗和响应延迟。OpenAI 因此建议尽量保留原始对话历史，并使用官方提供的上下文压缩接口。

items.body:
Meta Muse 隐私问题接连曝光：乱读加密消息、疑似串号，甚至擅自花钱

路透社查看了 Meta 员工的 20 多条内部反馈，发现 AI 智能体 Muse 出了不少离谱的问题。

一名员工只是在跟 Muse 聊钓鱼天气，它却突然报出两笔银行余额：Capital One 账户有 2722.58 美元，嘉信理财账户有 5899.57 美元。该员工表示，自己从没提供过银行信息，也没跟 Muse 聊过银行的事，怀疑它把别人的信息发给了自己。

另一名员工发现，Muse 突然提醒她回复姐姐在 Signal 上的私信。但她根本没有把 Signal 连接到 Muse，也不记得授权它读取其他应用。

路透社随后联合 Signal 和 AI Now Institute 进行了测试，确认 Muse 确实能绕过官方连接器，读到 Signal 的聊天内容。

在 Android 手机上，Muse 可以通过通知权限读取私信；在 Mac 上，它能调用系统辅助功能和截图工具，直接查看聊天界面。相同操作在 iPhone 上没能成功。

Muse 把用户之前授予的系统权限，用到了用户根本没想到的地方。即使没有连接 Signal，它也能通过这些权限拿到聊天内容。

Muse 还闯过其他祸。有员工反映，它擅自预订了不能退款的 Airbnb 住宿。还有人称，它把自己的宠物保险从每月 200 美元升级到了 888 美元，钱也没能追回来。

Meta 回应称，这些只是个别事件。那些看起来像是把别人信息发错账号的消息，很多其实是 AI 自己编出来的，公司已经修复了相关问题，员工测试的部分功能也并未向普通用户开放。

items.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
items.summary: OpenAI’s layered approach to adversarial distillation combines model training, safeguards, detection, and enforcement to protect against capability extraction.
items.body:
November 20, 2026

How we’re addressing safety risks of distillation and lessons we’ve learned for strengthening safeguards across the industry.

As frontier AI models become more capable, safeguards play an increasingly important role in how they can be used responsibly. Adversarial distillation creates a path for bad actors to reproduce these capabilities without appropriate safeguards. An actor may use a frontier model’s outputs without authorization to train another model with similar capabilities, then deploy it without comparable protections. For instance, an adversary might distill a model’s cyber capabilities and use the resulting model to help carry out cyberattacks that the original model would have refused to assist with or that its safeguards would have blocked.

We’re sharing how OpenAI detects and disrupts adversarial distillation, how we’ve strengthened protections for our models’ protected reasoning, and what we’ve learned that can help strengthen defenses across the industry.

Our approach to adversarial distillation combines adversarial testing, model training, classifiers, and API-level protections with investigations into coordinated attempts to extract model capabilities. These updated safeguards align more closely with those we use for biology and cybersecurity.

We place particular emphasis on preventing attackers from extracting our models’ protected reasoning: the intermediate steps a model generates internally while working toward an answer, known as its chain-of-thought. These traces can contain information the final answer leaves out, making them especially valuable training data for another model.

We’ve strengthened our defenses against protected reasoning extraction in GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol. In an internal adaptive evaluation using strong automated red-teaming, we tested whether attackers could recover protected reasoning the model had generated while answering an earlier prompt. The average attack success rate fell from 54.0% against GPT‑6 Astra with its original safeguards to 0.2% against GPT‑6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards.

Distillation is a common machine-learning technique in which one model learns from data produced by another. For example, a model can learn from another model’s answers, its reasoning, or its judgments about which answers are better and why. Beyond intellectual property concerns, unauthorized distillation poses serious safety risks. Through adversarial distillation, a second model can learn advanced frontier capabilities without inheriting the safeguards that govern how the original model can use them.

The concern is especially clear in dual-use domains like cybersecurity and biology. A model that helps defenders find vulnerabilities in software could also help an attacker exploit them; a model that assists with biological research could also help someone develop a harmful pathogen. If such capabilities were transferred to a model with weaker safeguards, it may provide assistance that the original model would have refused, or that the original safeguards would have blocked.

Our models help users with coding and defensive cybersecurity tasks. A second model trained on many of those benign outputs may learn skills that also apply to offensive cybersecurity tasks. To better understand this, we study how distillation, especially involving reasoning traces, may transfer risky cyber capabilities.

In this setting, the model that produces the training data is called the teacher, and the model that learns from it is called the student. In an internal study on how cyber capabilities transfer, we used the content normally visible to users—final responses, reasoning summaries, and tool interactions—as our baseline for distillation, and tested how much additional cyber capability transfers when the student has access to the teacher’s exact reasoning traces.

We started each training run from the same pretrained student model. We created a supervised fine-tuning dataset consisting primarily of trajectories from Astra-level teacher models working on coding and defensive cybersecurity tasks. Each trajectory includes all of the steps a model takes as it works through a task, including any tool interactions and its final response. We evaluated each student after fine-tuning and again after a lightweight round of reinforcement learning in cybersecurity and coding environments.

After supervised fine-tuning, the student trained on exact reasoning traces generally outperformed the student trained on reasoning summaries. After reinforcement learning, the exact-trace student still scored higher at the largest inference budget tested on both benchmarks shown, while the summary-trained student scored higher at lower budgets.

Our cyber distillation results suggest that protecting reasoning traces can limit cyber capability transfer, even when the underlying task is one allowed under our usage policies. Across many such interactions, exact reasoning traces can teach a student skills that generalize beyond the tasks the teacher originally performed. We will continue studying how much additional capability transfers across different student models and distillation training recipes.

We defend against adversarial distillation at two complementary levels of our safeguard stack. At the request level, model behavior, classifier checks, and API controls limit reasoning trace extraction. At the campaign level, we look for patterns in request-level and account-level signals that can reveal coordinated extraction attempts. In turn, attacks uncovered in investigations become examples for training and testing our safeguards.

Adversarial training teaches models to recognize reasoning extraction attempts and refuse to disclose protected reasoning, while preserving responses to legitimate requests for explanations and assistance. Adversarial training examples come from successful attacks identified through internal automated red-teaming, investigations, and responsible disclosures of potential security weaknesses from outside researchers or industry partners.

We use input classifiers to detect attempts to extract protected reasoning, and output classifiers to detect leaks of protected reasoning in assistant messages and tool-call arguments. These safeguards apply to both streaming and non-streaming responses.

Tool-call coverage is important because a model can expose protected reasoning in a tool’s arguments without including it in its final answer. Output classifiers can block suspected leaks before that content reaches the caller.

API-level protections restrict how protected reasoning can be reused across interactions and models. Our September disclosure described attacks that moved encrypted reasoning from one conversation into another and asked the model to reveal the reasoning in user-readable form. How we’re addressing safety risks of distillation and lessons we’ve learned for strengthening safeguards across the industry.

Our approach to adversarial distillation combines adversarial testing, model training, classifiers, and API-level protections with investigations into coordinated attempts to extract model capabilities. These updated safeguards align more closely with those we use for biology and cybersecurity.

We place particular emphasis on preventing attackers from extracting our models’ protected reasoning: the intermediate steps a model generates internally while working toward an answer, known as its chain-of-thought. These traces can contain information the final answer leaves out, making them especially valuable training data for another model.

Our models help users with coding and defensive cybersecurity tasks. A second model trained on many of those benign outputs may learn skills that also apply to offensive cybersecurity tasks.
